title: Deathrow
subtitle: A disc sport with room for a fight

body: Deathrow is Southend Interactive's Xbox sports game, first released in Europe on 18 October 2002. Its invented sport, Blitz, puts two teams of four into an arena where scoring and fighting are both legitimate routes to victory. Players carry and pass an energised disc before throwing it through the opposition's raised hoop. A team can win on points or by knocking out every opponent. That second possibility changes the meaning of defence: a player away from the disc can still influence the result by removing someone who would otherwise contest it.

Passing opens routes through a defence, while punches, kicks and throws can disrupt the players trying to close them. Fighting consumes health, and an exhausted competitor leaves the match until substitutions become available between rounds. Team members can also hurt one another, so indiscriminate aggression creates its own danger. Credits earned from goals, knockouts and crowd-pleasing play support upgrades and recruitment through the campaign. The player develops a team whose strengths should match the preferred balance between moving the disc quickly and imposing physical control over the arena.

Development began as an online PC project before Southend shifted to Xbox and its graphics capabilities. Local and System Link multiplayer supported contests beyond the campaign, though Xbox Live play was absent. Critics praised the energetic action and the unusual sporting idea, while noting the steep learning curve. Strong reviews did not produce enough sales for a sequel. Deathrow remains distinctive because its violence changes the tactical situation rather than merely decorating the sport: every injured player alters the passing options and defensive pressure available to both teams.
